source.title: A solution to an open problem on Mathieu series posed by Hoorfar and Qi

accepted.question_text: For the Mathieu series S(r) = sum over n >= 1 of 2n/(n^2 + r^2)^2, defined for every real r > 0, what are the best possible constants a and b such that the double inequality 1/(r^2 + 1/2 - (4r^2 + 1)/(12(r^2 + a))) < S(r) < 1/(r^2 + 1/2 - (4r^2 + 1)/(12(r^2 + b))) holds for all r > 0, under the previously established necessary bounds a <= 3/2 and b >= 1/4?
accepted.context_brief: Best constants for Mathieu series bounds

evidence.quote: We consider the series S(r) = sum n>=1 2n/(n2 + r2)2, r > 0 called Mathieu's series in the literature.

Our main purpose is to prove the following problem proposed by A. Hoorfar and F. Qi [5]: find the best possible constants a and b such that (1.2) 1/(r2 + 1/2 - (4r2 + 1)/(12(r2 + a))) < S(r) < 1/(r2 + 1/2 - (4r2 + 1)/(12(r2 + b))) holds true for all r > 0. They showed that a <= 3/2 and b >= 1/4. The following theorem gives a complete answer.
Theorem 1.1. For any real number r > 0, the inequality (1.2) holds with the best possible constants a = zeta(3)/(6zeta(3) - 6) = 0.9915168156... and b = 13/30.
